findings.summary: _set_root_namespace fails to detect the end of a multi-line docstring — in_docstring stays True forever after entering, causing all subsequent content (imports, assignments) to be silently dropped
findings.failure_scenario: An __init__.py containing '\"\"\"Multi-line\ndocstring\"\"\"\nfrom ._version import VERSION' has in_docstring=True from line 1 and never toggles back (the closing \"\"\" on line 2 does not start with triple quotes, so no toggle occurs; a closing \"\"\" alone on a line does start with \"\"\" but the condition also requires NOT ending with \"\"\", which is False — so still no toggle). All lines after the docstring are skipped, content is empty, and _set_root_namespace returns None. discover_namespace then falls back to the next __init__.py or ultimately to name.replace('-', '.') — producing an incorrect namespace. For azure-eventhub-checkpointstoreblob, this could yield 'azure.eventhub.checkpointstoreblob' instead of 'azure.eventhub.extensions.checkpointstoreblob', silently breaking sphinx docs, mypy/pyright type checking, and import verification.

findings.summary: _set_root_namespace does not exclude single-line triple-quoted docstrings from the content list, inflating the line count and causing false 'substantial content' detection
findings.failure_scenario: An __init__.py containing '\"\"\"Azure SDK.\"\"\"\n__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)' has the single-line docstring incorrectly added to content (because it starts AND ends with \"\"\", so the toggle condition 'starts but does not end' is False and in_docstring stays False; the line is not a #-comment so it passes the append filter). The extension line is also added, giving content 2 items. len(content) > 1 causes the function to return the module name, treating this namespace-extension-only file as substantial. The wrong (shallower) namespace is used.

findings.summary: _set_root_namespace does not filter blank/empty lines, which are appended to the content list and can inflate the line count past 1 for extension-only __init__.py files
findings.failure_scenario: An __init__.py with a blank line followed by '__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)' has the empty line (stripped to '') added to content because 'not "".startswith("#")' evaluates to True. Both the blank line and the extension line are in content, giving len(content) > 1, so the function incorrectly returns the module name instead of None. This causes discover_namespace to stop at this file and use the wrong namespace.

findings.summary: requires can be None when pyproject.toml [project] lacks a 'dependencies' key, causing TypeError on line 491 where None is iterated by map()
findings.failure_scenario: A pyproject.toml with a valid [project] section but no 'dependencies' key (which is optional per PEP 621) has project_config.get('dependencies') return None. Line 491 calls any(map(lambda x: ..., None)), which raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable. This crashes parse_pyproject for any dependency-free package using pyproject.toml. (Pre-existing bug; the setup.py path handles this with a [ ] default.)
